title: At a hard run boundary the final turn declares candidate_written true with no witnessed write in the retained stream; the broker correctly refuses the declaration, but the fault overwrites a terminal state the checkpoint had already settled

evidence.note: run_fault at campaign-evidence/runs/open_cake-1/events/000000000117.json: RunProtocolFault 'Claude candidate write lifecycle is incomplete', turn 8. The retained provider_stdout (campaign-evidence/objects/sha256/7d/7de9192d330530334c1e8a957062ee9a62f588d98f338f756a77080a939c14e2, 12 lines) is one clean exchange: thinking, a summary text reporting the turn-7 evaluation ('late scaling gave peak live 17 and 0.011621 ms / 3.166x'), a StructuredOutput tool_use declaring candidate_written true, its tool_result, one rate_limit_event (five_hour, allowed), then result is_error false subtype success. No Write call anywhere. Event 000000000118 is checkpoints_projected with state reached_no_qualified_candidate at provider_tokens exactly 3000000; event 000000000119 is run_terminal endpoint_observation missing, protocol_adherence provider_fault. terminal_provider_tokens 3277759.

same byte shape: turn 10, retained stream (objects/sha256/ed/edec7dd7b71de98da44b9b2dae51fa8f86597d06ebd9c8389587427e7df0b817) ends StructuredOutput candidate_written true with no Write, result success; observed_quota seven_day allowed_warning utilization 0.25 -- quota healthy, so the boundary, not the wall, is the trigger. terminal_provider_tokens 3217979.

third instance, turn 9, terminal_provider_tokens 3249745, observed_quota seven_day allowed_warning 0.26. Three of the eleven full-budget runs in the -d batch faulted this way (~27%); the eight that ended cleanly declared candidate_written consistently with the witnessed lifecycle at their own token-limit boundaries.

the first instance and the only five-hour-boundary one: turn 10, observed_quota five_hour allowed with overage rejected (resetsAt 1789476000), same exception message, turn-10 result itself successful. Its -d rerun under the same Revision completed cleanly as no_qualified_candidate, so the mismatch is not task-deterministic. momentum_sgd-d's clean terminal also shows the class does not require a code change to recover.

observation: Four runs faulted with 'Claude candidate write lifecycle is incomplete' after a successful CLI result: the boundary-exhausted final turn declares candidate_written true while its retained stream witnesses no write. The broker is right to refuse an unwitnessed declaration -- accepting it would let a turn claim work it did not do. The defect is ordering: in all four, the checkpoint projection had ALREADY settled the run's terminal state at the exact budget boundary (reached_no_qualified_candidate at provider_tokens 3000000 in the layernorm_backward_input-d case), and the post-hoc declaration check then converts that settled no_qualified outcome into provider_fault. Nothing scientific is lost -- search evidence is complete, no qualified endpoint existed at any of the four boundaries, and one of the three affected -d tasks' models even retained its final search finding in the stream -- but the terminal classification is wrong-shaped, and three tasks (layernorm_backward_input, rmsnorm_input_gradient, absmax_rescale) now have no clean terminal across three attempts each (quota wall, gateway window, boundary mismatch) purely through fault-class luck.
proposed_change: Order the boundary so a settled checkpoint wins: when the token-budget (or five-hour) boundary has produced a terminal checkpoint state, complete run_terminal from that checkpoint and record the unreconciled candidate_written declaration as a named protocol diagnostic on the terminal event, instead of raising RunProtocolFault after the fact. The declaration check itself is unchanged and still fails closed for any turn whose write lifecycle is incomplete WITHOUT a settled terminal behind it. Alternatively (or additionally) validate the declaration at the turn seam so the mismatch is a named refusal the author sees, not a post-run fault.
implemented_in: open-cake-ir@4dfed5fd (per ADR 0065; tick commit cfd3883f, reviewed merge tree-identical to 5154d7a5): ClaudeCandidateWriteUnwitnessed names the boundary shape at the parse seam, the adapter raises ProviderBoundaryDeclarationFault (fails closed as provider_fault in flight), and execution converts to the settled checkpoint terminal only when the final projected checkpoint is already settled, with a closed boundary_diagnostic marker on run_terminal beside the retained run_fault.
verification_plan: Protocol tick, replay-verified: replay the four cited fault streams under the successor and observe a no_qualified_candidate terminal carrying the diagnostic, with contract tests covering (a) settled-checkpoint boundary with an unreconciled declaration, (b) an incomplete write lifecycle with NO settled checkpoint still faulting, and (c) evidence sealed before the change replaying unchanged.

verified_by.scope: the four cited boundary faults and the conversion rule; the declaration check itself still fails closed for any turn whose write lifecycle is incomplete without a settled terminal behind it
verified_by.observed: All four cited stdouts reparse at the merge to the named shape under their own expected terminal documents: momentum_sgd turn 10 (v118-c) and absmax_rescale turn 9, layernorm_backward_input turn 8, rmsnorm_input_gradient turn 10 (v118-d). Their retained fault terminals are untouched -- the conversion is an execution-time act, so each cited run keeps the fault terminal it sealed and the settled-checkpoint conversion takes effect on the first campaign run at this Revision. The 4dfed5fd review confirmed the fail-closed properties independently: admission forces the final projected checkpoint to sit exactly at the limit, so a converted terminal's stop reason is necessarily the provider token limit and never the maximum-turns fallback; and an unconverted ProviderBoundaryDeclarationFault in flight records the ordinary provider_fault shape. Reviewer re-ran the two changed contract files at 5154d7a5 (65 passed).
verified_by.contracts: tests/contracts/test_claude_provider.py::test_budget_boundary_declaration_without_a_write_is_its_own_named_shape and ::test_boundary_declaration_adapter_fault_is_named_and_fails_closed; tests/contracts/test_provider_fault_usage.py::test_settled_checkpoint_outlives_a_budget_boundary_declaration_fault (settled checkpoint converts with the terminal marker and the natural provider_token_limit stop reason, and the Codex-contract synthetic campaign cannot carry the Claude marker -- the refusal asserts the contract scoping) and ::test_boundary_declaration_without_a_settled_checkpoint_stays_a_fault

verified_by.limits: OPEN VERIFICATION ITEM (carried from the 4dfed5fd review): the replay acceptance path for a converted terminal -- replay.py's boundary branch and replay_outcomes' boundary_converted logic driven to semantic_replay_passed true -- has no positive test; the settled-checkpoint contract test uses a Codex-contract fixture, asserts only the refusal, and does not yet confirm the refusal comes specifically from the contract-scoping check rather than an unrelated rule. Open until a positive replay test exists or the first live campaign at this Revision hits the boundary and its audit witnesses the converted terminal. Replay otherwise validates the marker by reparsing the retained fault stdout under the fault turn's expected terminal and requiring exactly one provider fault, exactly one provider_stdout, and the settled checkpoint; it does not retime anything. Minor, non-blocking, for a later tick: the boundary_diagnostic shape validation is written twice in store.py (seal and archive audit) and can be lifted into one function.
